evals.name: phased-pharmacy-with-ai
evals.prompt:
I'm building MediStock, an offline-first pharmacy management system for independent pharmacies in Indonesia. Here's the architecture:

- Local server runs on a mini-PC inside each pharmacy (SQLite, .NET API). Cashier tablets and pharmacist laptops connect over the pharmacy's WiFi.
- Optional cloud sync for chain owners with multiple branches — outbox pattern, last-write-wins for inventory, server-authoritative for prescriptions.
- 6-phase delivery: (1) local-server foundation + auth, (2) inventory + barcode scanning, (3) POS with cash-drawer reconciliation, (4) digital prescriptions with QR codes, (5) cloud sync + chain analytics, (6) AI assistant for drug-interaction checks (BYOK to OpenAI/Gemini).
- Multi-tenant: one cloud instance serves many pharmacy chains; data isolation by `EntityId`.
- Stores PII (patient phone, KTP national ID), PHI (prescriptions, allergies, drug history), financial (sales, controlled-substance audit). Indonesian narcotics regulation (Permenkes 3/2015) requires controlled-substance dispensing audit.
- Patients use a mobile app to view their prescriptions and request refills.

Can you do a full security threat model for this? I want something I can hand to my engineering team and have them work through phase by phase.
evals.expected_output: A single markdown threat model with: trust-boundary recap, sensitive-data inventory, STRIDE catalog (with system-specific attack vectors not generic web threats), AI/ML section (because phase 6 uses BYOK LLM), mitigations marked BLOCKING/REQUIRED, phase coverage matrix (1-6), out-of-scope pointers. Should reference Indonesian PDP Law and Permenkes 3/2015 for narcotics. Should NOT pad with non-applicable threats.

assertions.text: Includes a STRIDE catalog with all six categories (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege)
Includes a dedicated AI/ML threats section because phase 6 uses BYOK LLM
Includes a phase coverage matrix mapping threats to phases 1–6
References Indonesian regulations (at minimum Permenkes 3/2015 for narcotics; ideally also Indonesian PDP Law / UU PDP)
Includes a threat covering rogue server / mDNS or LAN spoofing on the pharmacy WiFi
Includes a threat covering prescription QR-code forgery, with a cryptographic-signature mitigation
Includes a cross-entity / multi-tenant data isolation failure threat with EntityId-scoped query mitigation
Mitigations are explicitly marked BLOCKING or REQUIRED
Includes a controlled-substance inventory manipulation threat tied to the Permenkes audit requirement
Includes a sync-related threat (outbox poisoning, last-write-wins clock abuse, or replay) given the system has cloud sync

evals.name: telemedicine-startup-no-phases
evals.prompt:
We just got our seed round for a telemedicine startup in the UK called Sereno. Quick description:

- Patients book video consults with GPs via our web app (Next.js) and iOS/Android (Flutter).
- Backend is a Node.js + Postgres monolith on AWS eu-west-1.
- We use Twilio for video, Stripe for payments, NHS Login for patient auth (OAuth/OIDC).
- Doctors authenticate with our own SSO + GMC number verification.
- We use OpenAI GPT-4 to auto-summarise consultation transcripts into clinical notes (the doctor reviews and edits before saving).
- We send prescriptions electronically via the EPS (Electronic Prescription Service) API.
- All clinical data stored in Postgres with column-level encryption for free-text fields.

We're not phased — it all ships at MVP. My investors want to see a security threat model before we go live. Can you produce one?
evals.expected_output: A markdown threat model. Should NOT include a phase coverage matrix (no phases) — instead a Component Coverage matrix or skip that section. Should include AI/ML threats (uses GPT-4 for summarisation). Should reference UK GDPR/DPA 2018, NHS DSP Toolkit, and DCB0129/DCB0160 if applicable. Specific threats around: NHS Login token handling, EPS prescription tampering, video session hijack, clinical-summary AI errors, GMC credential verification.

assertions.text: Includes a STRIDE catalog with all six categories (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege)
Includes a dedicated AI/ML threats section because the system uses GPT-4 for clinical-note summarisation
Does NOT include a phase coverage matrix (system is not phased — uses component coverage or omits the section)
References UK regulations (at minimum UK GDPR / DPA 2018; ideally NHS DSP Toolkit or DCB0129/DCB0160)
Includes an AI-summarisation hallucination / fabrication threat (T or AI04-style — affects clinical safety)
Includes an NHS Login OAuth/OIDC token-handling threat (PKCE, state, scope, or token replay)
Includes an EPS prescription submission tampering or replay threat with HMAC/signature mitigation
Includes a Twilio video session hijack or eavesdropping threat
Mitigations are explicitly marked BLOCKING or REQUIRED
Includes a doctor credential / GMC verification spoofing threat

evals.name: lab-information-system-no-ai
evals.prompt:
I'm the architect at MedLab Group, a chain of diagnostic labs in Saudi Arabia. We're building a new LIS (Lab Information System) to replace our 15-year-old vendor system. Stack:

- C# .NET 8 backend, SQL Server, Angular frontend.
- Hosted on-prem in our Riyadh data centre. No cloud, no offline mode.
- Integrates with: HL7 v2 from analyser instruments (chemistry, haematology, microbiology), DICOM for some imaging, FHIR API for hospital partners, SFDA reporting for notifiable diseases.
- Workflow: specimen collection → accessioning → instrument result → tech verification → pathologist verification (where required) → result release to ordering doctor + patient portal.
- Patient portal lets patients view their results once released.
- Roles: phlebotomist, lab tech, pathologist, doctor (external — accesses via FHIR), patient.
- Data: PHI (results, diagnoses, specimen chain of custody), PII (Iqama/national ID, phone), no payment data (billing is a separate system).
- No AI features. We don't do clinical decision support.

Can you do a security threat model? I want to focus on threats we'd realistically see, not generic web stuff.
evals.expected_output: A markdown threat model. Should NOT include an AI/ML section (no AI features in the system). Should NOT include phase coverage matrix (single release). Should include component coverage. Specific threats around: HL7 instrument tampering (forged results), DICOM PHI leakage, pathologist verification bypass, specimen chain of custody, FHIR API authorisation, patient-portal IDOR, on-prem ransomware. Should reference Saudi PDPL (Royal Decree M/19) and SFDA reporting requirements, NOT Egypt-specific or US HIPAA.

assertions.text: Includes a STRIDE catalog with all six categories (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege)
Does NOT include an AI/ML threats section (the system has no AI features)
Does NOT include a phase coverage matrix (single release — uses component coverage or omits the section)
References Saudi-specific regulations (Saudi PDPL Royal Decree M/19, SFDA reporting, or NPHIES); does NOT use HIPAA / US-specific compliance content
Includes an HL7 v2 instrument tampering / forged result injection threat (HL7 has no native auth)
Includes a DICOM metadata PHI leakage threat with redaction mitigation
Includes a pathologist verification state-machine bypass threat (Draft → Verified → Released)
Includes a patient-portal IDOR / horizontal escalation threat (Iqama enumeration or cross-patient access)
Includes a FHIR API authorisation / scope threat for external doctor access
Mitigations are explicitly marked BLOCKING or REQUIRED
